page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.45-360 is a compute instance within the flexible Ampere A4 family. Configured with 90 dedicated physical cores on the 64-bit Arm architecture (AmpereOne-M), it assigns one thread per core across all 90 vCPUs. System memory is sized at 360.0 GB, providing an exact ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, typical of a balanced general-purpose footprint. The configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and does not integrate local storage or discrete graphics accelerators.

Because each vCPU maps directly to a dedicated physical Arm core without simultaneous multithreading, workloads avoid hardware thread contention, delivering consistent per-core execution. The high core count combined with 360.0 GB of memory makes the platform effective for heavily parallel execution environments. However, systems requiring fast scratch space or ultra-low storage latency must rely entirely on remote network-attached block volumes due to the absence of bundled local NVMe drives.

From an efficiency standpoint, dedicated Arm-based silicon delivers dense compute throughput per physical core with moderate power and resource consumption relative to legacy x86 architectures. This setup suits highly parallel web services, microservice clusters, continuous integration compilation farms, container orchestration nodes, and distributed data processing pipelines that require predictable core isolation and balanced memory allocation.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.45-360 is an Arm-based flexible compute instance equipped with 90 dedicated physical cores powered by the AmpereOne-M processor architecture. The platform operates 90 vCPUs with a single thread per core, eliminating noisy-neighbor effects caused by simultaneous multithreading. It includes 360.0 GB of system memory, matching the standard balanced profile of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware GPU acceleration, requiring reliance on external block storage services for persistence. With its heavy parallel capacity and dedicated core allocation, the instance is engineered to support distributed microservices, software build pipelines, containerized application clusters, and batch data processing workloads that benefit from consistent multi-core Arm throughput.
